description: bstack governance hooks. Paths self-locate via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} so they survive reinstalls and are invisible to the skills CLI. The two hooks that WRITE <workspace>/.control UNCONDITIONALLY (knowledge-wakeup via leverage-ship-sensor; leverage-sensor at Stop) run through bstack-hook-guard.sh, which no-ops them outside a bstack-governed workspace so this personal-scope plugin never pollutes non-bstack repos. arc-continuation + autonomous-posture are session-scoped, self-guarding, and write nothing to the workspace, so they run unwrapped (wrapping them would false-negative the loop-stall logic when cwd is a nested non-governed repo). ask-origin-stamp-hook.sh also writes under <workspace>/.control (an ask's origin: block) but is NOT wrapped: its own bash-only prefilter (PASEO_AGENT_ID set, AND the raw tool-call JSON mentions `.control/asks/*.yaml`) already guarantees the path exists before python3 is even spawned, so the guard's `.control`-exists check would be a strictly redundant git spawn on every Write/Edit/MultiEdit in every session. l3-stability is source-guarded internally. test-lock-hook fail-opens on internal error (`bstack test-lock verify` in CI is the backstop). bstack-autoupdate is workspace-agnostic (global). Primitive map: SessionStart = P6 knowledge-wakeup + P7 autoupdate; Stop = P19 arc-continuation + loop-sensor; UserPromptSubmit = P19 autonomous-posture; PreToolUse = L3-G0 gate + P11 test-lock (blocks edits to tests committed under a Test-Lock: trailer); PostToolUse = BRO-2918 ask-origin-stamp (runs `ask_ledger.py stamp` on every Write/Edit/MultiEdit of a `.control/asks/*.yaml` file, so a new ask always names the session that raised it — never blocks; a stamp failure is swallowed).
